fields.h1: Build a Matrix Survey Question With Results for Every Row
fields.hero_description: Build a matrix survey question that rates several items on one scale and saves each row's answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Matrix Question
fields.features_subheading: A matrix asks several questions on one scale. Emergent builds the grid people answer and the table that keeps a score for each row.
fields.feature_1:
Rows and a scale from one prompt

Name the row items and the scale, such as five statements on a 5-point agree scale. Emergent builds the grid, and a later prompt adds a row or renames a column label.
fields.feature_2:
One row per screen on a phone

On a phone, respondents see one row at a time with the scale as large buttons, and nobody scrolls sideways. A laptop shows the full grid with the same rows and labels.
fields.feature_3:
Each row saved as its own value

The answer to every row lands in its own column of a database you own, with the label chosen and its number on the scale. Put this round's rows beside the last round's.
fields.feature_4:
Per-row averages and an alert

The dashboard shows the average and the share who agree for each row. Set a floor for any row, and the app sends an email or a Slack message when its average drops under it.
fields.feature_5:
Same-column answers flagged

Ask the app to flag any response that picks the same column in every row. The dashboard shows each row with and without those answers, and you decide whether they count.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can export

Each matrix survey Emergent builds is code. On paid plans, export it to your GitHub repository with the rows, the scale and the dashboard, and run the next round from your repo.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Grids and What Their Rows Showed
fields.tab_content_1:
93 agree on tools, while no other row falls under 149

Corriebrook Outfitters asks its store employees to rate five statements from Strongly disagree to Strongly agree, and 212 of the 240 answer. Just 93 agree that they have the tools to do the job. Every other row draws at least 149, so the operations lead puts new registers and scanners into next quarter's budget.
fields.tab_content_2:
An email goes out when breakfast falls to 3.2

Every Monday, Carrowmere Inn asks last week's guests to rate four parts of their stay on a 5-point satisfaction scale. When a row's weekly average falls below 3.5, the general manager gets an email. This week 86 guests answered and breakfast averaged 3.2. The kitchen added a hot dish to the menu before Saturday.
fields.tab_content_3:
58 answers pick one column all the way down

Notewell asks 640 users how often they use five features, on a scale from Never to Always. The app flags 58 answers that chose Always in all five rows. Without them, only 52 of the other 582 pick Often or Always for export, and the team moves export down the roadmap.
fields.tab_content_4:
Residents put restrooms before any other project

The Ashby Hollow parks board asks residents to rate five park projects by importance, from 1 to 5, and 1,130 answer on their phones. Each project gets its own screen with large buttons. New restrooms average 4.4 out of 5, the highest of the five, and the board puts them first in next year's spending plan.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Matrix Survey Question
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a matrix survey question whose rows share one scale and whose results you can act on row by row.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick what every row is rated on
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Keep each row to one idea
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Cap the grid near five by five
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the one measure the whole grid uses, such as agreement or how often. If two items need different scales, like a 1 to 5 rating and a yes or no, they belong in separate questions. A matrix works only when one set of column labels fits every row.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write Fair schedules, not Fair schedules and pay. A row that joins two ideas gets one answer for both, and nobody can tell which one moved the score. Read the rows aloud before you build, and split any row with an and in the middle.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose the columns and their labels before the rows go in. A 5-point agree scale with a neutral middle suits statements, and a Never to Always scale suits habits. Label every column in words: a 4 should mean the same thing to every respondent.
fields.howto_step_4_des: SurveyMonkey suggests showing 5 or fewer items in a matrix, and 5 or fewer response options. With nine items, split them into two grids by topic, such as pay and schedules in one and tools and training in the other.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell Emergent the rows, the column labels, and who answers, in plain sentences. Emergent builds the grid, the table behind it, and the dashboard in one pass. Mention how people get the link, such as an email to every store, and Emergent builds the invitation too.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it with five people on phones
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the survey to five people and watch at least two of them answer on a phone. Ask anyone who taps the same column all the way down why they did it. Then open the table and match each stored answer to what they tapped.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the results one row at a time
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sort the rows by the count who agree and start at the bottom. Compare each row with the same row in the last round to see which one moved. Pick one low row to act on, and say in the next invitation what changed because of it.

faq_plan.a: A matrix survey question is a closed-ended question that asks respondents to evaluate one or more row items using the same set of column choices. The rows are the things being rated, such as five workplace statements, and the columns are the shared scale. Each row gets its own answer.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up matrix survey question?
faq_plan.a: Describe the rows and the scale in one prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder, for example five statements rated by every store employee. Emergent builds the question and a dashboard with a result for each row. Adjust the wording by prompt, then send a test to a few people before the full launch.

faq_plan.q: Can you provide some examples of matrix survey questions?
faq_plan.ref: Can you provide some examples of matrix survey questions?

prov.original: Can you provide some examples of matrix survey questions?

faq_plan.a: Yes. A staff survey rates statements like I have the tools to do my job and My schedule is fair on an agree scale. A hotel asks guests to rate check-in, room, breakfast, and housekeeping on a satisfaction scale. A software team asks how often users open export and search, with frequency labels as the columns. A grid can also use checkboxes to allow more than one answer per row.

faq_plan.q: Where does a matrix survey question belong in the question order?
faq_plan.a: Put it in the middle, after the short questions that warm people up and before any open comment box. If the survey starts with screening survey questions, keep those first, so only people who qualify ever reach the grid. Follow the matrix with one open question that asks about its lowest row, while the ratings are still fresh.

faq_plan.q: When should you avoid a matrix survey question?
faq_plan.a: Skip the grid when the items need different scales, such as a rating for one and a yes or no for another. Split it when the list runs past five or six rows: a long grid is where people start tapping the same answer down the whole page. A single item with a follow-up, such as why did you rate breakfast low, also reads better as its own question.

faq_plan.q: Do matrix survey questions work well on phones?
faq_plan.a: They work when the layout changes for a small screen. In SurveyMonkey, a wide matrix on a phone may have respondents scroll to the right to see all of the available column choices. Qualtrics has a Mobile friendly option that formats matrix table statements into an accordion so they can all fit comfortably on 1 screen. Test your own grid on a phone before it goes out.

faq_plan.q: Can one matrix survey question rate every stage of a trip?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when every stage can share one scale. List check-in, boarding, seat comfort, and the cabin crew as rows, with Very dissatisfied to Very satisfied as the columns. A full set of airline survey questions would add an open question about the worst moment of the trip and a single question on whether the traveler would fly with you again.

faq_plan.q: What is straight-lining in a matrix survey question?
faq_plan.a: Straight-lining is when respondents select the same response for each item without careful consideration of each row. Write one row in the reverse direction, such as My workload is too heavy among positive statements, to make a careless pattern easier to spot. The app Emergent builds can tag those responses and keep them in the data for you to judge.

faq_plan.q: How do you analyze matrix survey question results?
faq_plan.a: Treat each row as its own question: count the answers in each column, then report the average or the share in the top two boxes for that row. Rank the rows to find the weakest, and check each row against its own result from the previous round. The app Emergent builds tags every saved answer with its round, in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Is every matrix survey question a rating scale?
faq_plan.a: No. A rating scale is one kind of matrix, and SurveyMonkey describes its Rating Scale question, commonly known as a Likert Scale, as a variation of the Matrix question. A matrix can also use frequency labels or checkboxes. Post meeting survey questions that rate the agenda, the length, and the follow-up on one agree scale are a Likert set laid out as a grid.
